primary.thesis: Two things work against the high strikes. First, timing: Ink is the Ethereum L2 built by Kraken on the OP Stack. Its INK token was announced, but as of 2026-09-30 the market is still open, so the token has not launched. Only three months remain before the Dec 31, 2026 deadline, and any case where it misses the deadline resolves every rung No. Second, valuation if it does launch: recent L2 and chain tokens have mostly listed at FDVs between the high hundreds of millions and a few billion, then sold off on airdrop recipients' selling in the first 24 hours. Ink has modest onchain activity and TVL compared with Base or Arbitrum. On day one it would more likely price between about $300M and $1.5B than above $2B. So the thesis is No on the upper rungs, which win both when there is no launch and when the launch is ordinary.

basket.reason: Wins if the token does not launch by year-end, or if it launches at a sub-$1B FDV, which is plausible for a mid-tier L2 hit by airdrop selling on day one.
A $2B+ FDV one day after launch would need Blast/Linea-level hype on top of an on-time launch. Both conditions have to hold together.
$3B+ is at the top end of recent L2 launches. That makes it the least likely outcome and the one most exposed to the timing risk.

failure_narrative: Kraken, possibly after an IPO and wanting to show the Ink ecosystem is worth something, pushes the token out in Q4 2026. It could do this with a large airdrop to Kraken exchange users, a low circulating float, and same-day listings on Kraken and other major exchanges (Binance, Coinbase, Bybit). This happens during a broad crypto rally with strong demand for L2 and exchange-affiliated tokens. Because the float is thin, a small circulating market cap turns into an FDV of $1B-$3B+ at 4pm ET the next day. All three No positions lose.
hedge_thesis: The worlds where the basket loses are crypto risk-on worlds: ETH and L2 tokens are rallying, exchange-affiliated assets trade at a premium, and Kraken has good reason to monetise its chain and has the market depth to support a high listing price. In those same worlds, other bets would tend to be winning: Ethereum and major L2 tokens (OP, ARB) trade higher, Coinbase and newly listed Kraken equity outperform, and bitcoin posts year-end highs. The link is that a high-FDV Ink launch requires strong liquidity and speculative demand across crypto markets. Instruments that pay when crypto rises in Q4 2026 therefore pay off exactly when my short on the valuation tail fails.
